newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends up, March at three-week high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends up, March at three-week high.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures racked up further gains Wednesday as continued trade and speculative buying lifted the market to three-week highs, dealers said.
Most-active March ended $16 higher at $1,394 a tonne after trading from $1,396 to $1,382. Spot December ended $6 higher at $1,340, while back months rose $14 to $15.
While some market participants reckoned the market's strong performances the last two sessions may mark the end of a recent downswing, others are less certain.

"Obviously, the market has picked up but I do not believe it is a genuine change in sentiment," Prudential Securities analyst Arthur Stevenson said. "I think the market has finally discounted various negative factors, such as anticipated Ivory Coast arrivals."
Cocoa continued to be helped by currency considerations, Stevenson said. As the strong Sterling may have prompted some arbitrage buying of cheaper dollar-denominated CSCE futures.

Technically, traders said $1,400 provided strong psychological resistance for March delivery, with a chart gap between $1,404 and $1,408 seen as the next upside hurdle. To the downside, a gap formed today from $1,382 and Tuesday's high of $1,379 was seen as support.
The day's volume reached an estimated 9,603 lots.
